clue.text: US city is unusually grandiose overlooking river

indicators.note: to overlook something is to ignore or leave it out, so a letter is dropped
done in an unusual way means not in the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river, and it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A tourist finds an American city unusually showy, perched above its river.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from GRANDIOSE to leave GANDIOSE, then rearrange those eight letters to get SAN DIEGO.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: Rising section of fortified site needs regular repairs

blocks.note: rising means going up
the keep is the strongest inner tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Part of an old castle wall is climbing upward and requires constant patching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like it describes the section, but it simply supplies UP; the keep is the main tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the ongoing maintenance needed to keep a building or object in good condition.

clue.text: Relaxed group of students entering fashionable area on lake

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: a form is a school class
what is in is in fashion
A is the abbreviation for area
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A laid-back class of pupils wanders into a trendy lakeside district.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is called a form; the class goes inside, between the first two pieces and the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal and relaxed both describe a casual manner free of ceremony or strict rules.

clue.text: Band of singers or such at work

indicators.note: something at work is being processed or worked on, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of vocalists, or something like it, busy on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The innocent filler words 'or such' are the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is an organised group singing together, as in an opera or choir.

clue.text: Smart agent grabbing short sleep

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: A clever operative steals a quick doze on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' belongs to the description of the sleep, not a signal to trim anything; the agent is split after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy dresser is smart, stylish and sharp in appearance.

clue.text: French composer keeps finale to another work of parody

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the final letter of the following word is used
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the rest

blocks.note: Erik Satie, French composer of the Gymnopedies
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A French composer holds on to the ending for another of his mocking pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Erik Satie is the composer; R goes between his I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses ridicule and exaggeration to mock, much as a parody imitates to poke fun.

clue.text: A new tiresome task cut short for news presenter

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a chore is a dull job

explanation.surface: A dull new duty is trimmed back to suit a television newsreader.
explanation.walkthrough: N for new is a standard abbreviation; the household job loses only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter who hosts a news broadcast, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Demarcated group rejecting leader in criminal enterprise

indicators.note: rejecting the leader means throwing out whoever is at the front, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a bracket is a category or band, such as an income bracket, with set limits

explanation.surface: A defined set of people turns on its boss within a gang's operation.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACKET minus its first letter B leaves RACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme for making money, such as extortion or fraud.

clue.text: Prepare round figure in part of a theatre

blocks.note: to dress food or a wound is to prepare it
a circle is a round shape

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a round shape somewhere in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round figure' tempts towards O or a number like a hundred, but here it is a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first raised tier of seating in a theatre, above the stalls.

clue.text: Heavy food? Eccentric gets to eat an excessive amount

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of their usual order
eating takes something inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: taken as written
OD is short for overdose, an excessive amount of a drug

explanation.surface: Stodgy dishes: an oddball keeps overeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' reads as a noun for a person, but it signals rearranging GETS into ST-GE, which then takes in OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is a British word for filling, starchy, heavy food such as suet puddings.

clue.text: It might feature cases on an estate?

definitions.text: It might feature cases on an estate?

blocks.note: surface reading: legal cases about a property or country estate
setter's reading: suitcases carried on top of an estate car

explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British name for a station wagon, and cases are luggage strapped on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a frame fixed on top of a vehicle for carrying luggage and other bulky items.

clue.text: Drive from university rector, for example, after retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
R is the abbreviation for rector
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Motivation drawn from a university head once he has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rector, for example' looks like one phrase but splits into R and EG; only EG is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and urge are synonyms for an inner push or strong desire to do something.

clue.text: Free ticket for all to see amid revised terms gets to appear adequate

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are reorganised
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a pass lets you in without paying
taken as written
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A complimentary ticket, open to everyone, within renegotiated conditions turns out to be good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a U-rated film is suitable for everyone; TERMS reshuffled as M-STER takes that U after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is an idiom meaning to meet the required standard or be acceptable.

clue.text: Pub found by green, say, showing distinctive features of a place

blocks.note: a local is the pub nearest your home, the one you regularly drink in
green is an example of a colour

explanation.surface: A pub beside the village green shows off what makes the area special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a village green but is a colour; in Britain your local is your regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Local colour is the idiom for the customs, scenery and character that give somewhere its individual atmosphere.

clue.text: Everybody in church retains a friendly relationship

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one letter is held inside the rest

blocks.note: everybody means all
taken as written
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone in a congregation keeps up good relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but supplies IN; ALL-IN-CE then takes A between I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit between friendly parties.

clue.text: Word aunt misused proves inappropriate

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative who uses a term wrongly turns out to be out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proves' just joins the two halves; all eight letters of the first two words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means improper or unseemly, behaviour that is not fitting for the situation.

clue.text: Sound of small seal or young swan

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

blocks.note: a signet is a small seal, often set in a ring

explanation.surface: The noise of a baby seal, or perhaps a little swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small seal' suggests a baby sea animal, but it is a signet, the seal on a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnet is the specific name for an immature swan, from the Latin for swan.

clue.text: Ape skirts middle of land in covering of a forest

indicators.note: the middle means the central part, so only the central letters are used
to skirt is to go around the edge, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate or copy
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A primate moves around the heart of the country under the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' reads as the animal, which fits a forest, but it is the verb meaning imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopy is the upper layer of a forest formed by the spreading crowns of trees.

clue.text: On the whole, danger ably diverted

indicators.note: diverted means sent along a different route, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Overall, a threat was skilfully headed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the definition at the front from the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning generally or in most respects, considering everything together.

clue.text: Lately discovered radio operator in London borough

blocks.note: something recently found is new
a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A wireless operator recently found living in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Newham is a borough in east London, home of the 2012 Olympic Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Newham is one of the thirty-two administrative districts that make up Greater London.

clue.text: Anticipate times taken over exercise in English court

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: x is the multiplication sign
PE is physical education
E is the abbreviation for English
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone foresees fines for a gym session held in an English courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken over' means placed on top of, so the multiplication sign comes first; the pair then sits inside English court.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect is to regard something as likely to happen, which is what anticipating means.

clue.text: Some hate amateurish group of players

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a part taken from inside the words

blocks.note: runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A few people loathe a bunch of clumsy, unskilled sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the first two words after the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a side of players who compete together in a sport or game.

clue.text: Cocktail currently taken by graduate and learner in confines of school

indicators.note: confines are the boundaries, so only the outermost letters are kept
placed in something means put inside it, so the earlier pieces go within the outer pair

blocks.note: currently means at present, now
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A drink currently being enjoyed by a graduate and a student within the school grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from British learner-driver plates; the three middle pieces sit between the first and last letters of school.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a mixed drink, classically advocaat with lemonade and lime, popular at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: One detained by expression of admiration in meeting for discussion

blocks.note: a POW is a prisoner of war
wow is an exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: A captive is held after someone gasps in awe during a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detained by' looks like a container instruction, but 'One detained' is a whole prisoner, placed by the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal word for a conference or get-together to talk something over.

clue.text: Hypnotic state affected Cretan

indicators.note: affected means altered or influenced, so the letters are changed around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Crete under the influence of hypnosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like it describes the islander's state, but it tells you to rearrange his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious condition like that induced by hypnotism, unaware of surroundings.

clue.text: Son far from straight in making complaint in the main?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
something curvy bends a lot

explanation.surface: A crooked son grumbles, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the open sea, where sailors once suffered scurvy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin C, was the classic illness of seafarers on long voyages.
